paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the identification, development and commercialization of differentiated medicines to address the unmet medical needs of patients with cancers. We seek to utilize our team's deep drug development experience to maximize the potential of our lead product candidate, firmonertinib, and advance a pipeline of novel therapeutics, such as next-generation antibody drug conjugates, including ARR-217 (MRG007), through approval and commercialization in patients suffering from cancer, with an initial focus on solid tumors. Firmonertinib is currently being evaluated in multiple clinical trials across a range of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations (EGFRm) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We are conducting a pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial of firmonertinib in treatment naive, or first-line, patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFRm NSCLC with exon 20 insertion mutations and a pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial of firmonertinib in first-line patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFRm NSCLC with P-loop and-alpha-c-helix compressing (PACC) mutations. We are conducting a Phase 1 clinical trial of ARR-217 in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors.

We received Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) for firmonertinib for first line EGFRm NSCLC with exon 20 insertion from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in October 2023, and Orphan Drug Designation for treatment of NSCLC with EGFRm or human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) mutations or human epidermal growth factor receptor 4 (HER4) mutations in February 2024. A product candidate can receive BTD if preliminary clinical evidence indicates that the product candidate, alone or in combination with one or more other drugs, may demonstrate substantial improvement over existing therapies on one or more clinically significant endpoints, such as substantial treatment effects observed early in clinical development. For drugs that have received BTD, interaction and communication between the FDA and the sponsor can help to identify the most efficient path for development, although BTD may not result in a faster development process, review or approval and does not increase the likelihood that the product candidate will ultimately receive FDA approval for any indication.

In 2021, we licensed from Shanghai Allist Pharmaceuticals, Co. Ltd (Allist) the right to develop and commercialize firmonertinib worldwide, with the exception of greater China, which includes mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. Firmonertinib is an investigational, novel, EGFR mutant-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that we are developing for the treatment of NSCLC patients across a broader set of EGFR mutations (EGFRm) than are currently served by approved EGFR TKIs. Firmonertinib is currently only approved and commercially distributed by Allist in China as a first-line therapy to treat classical EGFRm NSCLC. The FDA has not approved firmonertinib for any use. We selected firmonertinib for global development against nonclassical, or uncommon, mutations based on preliminary reductions in tumor size observed in seven out of ten patients with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations treated with firmonertinib in the ongoing Phase 1b clinical trial, the FAVOUR trial, conducted by Allist in China, and preclinical activity in PACC mutations, each a subtype of uncommon mutation. In a subsequent interim data readout from the FAVOUR trial of firmonertinib administered at 240 mg once daily in first-line patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFRm NSCLC with exon 20 insertion mutations, 79% of patients (n=22 out of 28 patients) were observed to experience a reduction in tumor size of at least 30%. In a final analysis from the Phase 1b FURTHER trial of firmonertinib, which included a cohort of EGFRm NSCLC with PACC mutations, we observed 16.0 months median progression free survival (mPFS) with firmonertinib 240 mg in first-line, confirmed overall response rate (cORR) 68.2% (n=15 out of 22 1L patients at 240mg) and duration of response (DOR) 14.6 months, and confirmed CNS (central nervous system) responses with firmonertinib including complete responses (CRs).

As one of the most prevalent cancers in the world, lung cancer imposes a significant global burden on human health, and EGFRm NSCLC represents a significant proportion of those affected. Despite progress in the therapeutic landscape for EGFRm NSCLC, many patients, particularly those with uncommon mutations, such as exon 20 insertions or PACC mutations, are underserved by existing treatments. In an interim data readout from the FAVOUR trial of firmonertinib administered at 240 mg once daily in first-line patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFRm NSCLC with exon 20 insertion mutations, 79% of patients (n=22 out of 28 patients) were observed to experience a reduction in tumor size of at least 30% from the baseline in a patient without evidence of progression as measured by Response Evaluation

Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1 criteria. This measurement of reduction is the threshold in this trial for a partial response and for inclusion in determination of the overall response rate (ORR), which is the primary endpoint of this trial. In the same interim data readout, those 79% of patients were observed to experience a 15.2 month median DOR. Interim results may not be indicative of final results; however, we believe these interim clinical results underscore firmonertinib's potential in patients whose tumors contain an uncommon EGFRm.

We are currently conducting a pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial, the FURVENT clinical trial, in first-line locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous EGFRm NSCLC patients with exon 20 insertion mutations and we expect topline data from this trial in mid-2026. Additionally, we are conducting a pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial, the ALPACCA clinical trial, in first-line locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous EGFRm NSCLC patients PACC mutations. In September 2025, our final Phase 1b PACC data reported 68.2% of patients (n=15 out of 22 1L patients at 240 mg) were observed to experience a confirmed reduction in tumor size of at least 30% from the baseline without evidence of progression as measured by RECIST 1.1 criteria. The confirmed mPFS in these patients was 16.0 months.

Since our inception in 2021, we have assembled a robust oncology pipeline by leveraging our global network and our experience in business development transactions. In 2021, we licensed from Allist the right to develop and commercialize firmonertinib worldwide, with the exception of greater China, which includes mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. Also in 2021, we entered into a research collaboration, as amended, with Aarvik Therapeutics, Inc. (Aarvik) to leverage its proprietary multi-target, multivalent, site-specific conjugation antibody platform to discover next-generation antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) with improved activity and safety over single target bivalent ADCs. In 2024, we entered into a collaboration agreement with Jiangsu Alphamab Biopharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. (Alphamab), a wholly owned subsidiary of Alphamab Oncology, to discover, develop and commercialize novel ADCs for the treatment of cancers globally, with the exception of greater China, which includes mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. In January 2025, we entered into an Exclusive License Agreement (the Lepu Biopharma Agreement) with Lepu Biopharma Co. Ltd. (Lepu Biopharma) pursuant to which Lepu Biopharma granted us the right to develop and commercialize ARR-217 (MRG007), a CD-H17-targeting ADC for gastrointestinal cancers outside greater China, which includes mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan.

We plan to continue to engage in business development activities to source additional innovative therapeutics in areas currently underserved by approved therapies. This broader strategy includes evaluating research collaborations, partnerships and licensing arrangements intended to expand our development pipeline of differentiated and next-generation oncology assets. Currently approved EGFR TKIs have achieved considerable commercial success and have become the standard of care for patients with NSCLC with classical EGFRm which comprise approximately 69% of all EGFRm NSCLC patients. However, many of these therapies, including AstraZeneca plc's (AstraZeneca) third-generation EGFR TKI, osimertinib (TAGRISSO®), are minimally active against or not approved for use in a significant portion of NSCLC patients with uncommon EGFRm. This unmet need leaves many EGFRm NSCLC patients with few effective treatment options. Firmonertinib is currently approved and commercially distributed by Allist in China as a first-line therapy to treat classical EGFRm NSCLC. However, firmonertinib was designed to have strong inhibitory activity, not only against classical EGFRm, but also against uncommon EGFRm, such as exon 20 insertion and PACC mutations which together account for approximately 22% of EGFRm NSCLC.

To date, firmonertinib has been evaluated in multiple clinical trials with an aggregate patient population of over 1,000 patients against a broad range of EGFRm NSCLC, including both classical and uncommon EGFRm. Based on the results of preclinical and clinical trials conducted to date, we believe that firmonertinib has the potential to retain many of the key advantages of third-generation EGFR TKIs compared to first- and second-generation EGFR TKIs, including overcoming T790M mutations that confer resistance to earlier generation TKIs, while also targeting a broader set of EGFRm. In 2022, Allist reported the results of its FURLONG clinical trial, a double blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 clinical trial of firmonertinib in first-line NSCLC patients with classical EGFRm. In FURLONG, firmonertinib was compared with the first-generation EGFR TKI, gefitinib, and demonstrated superior progression free survival (PFS) over gefitinib, showing a median PFS of 20.8 months versus 11.1 months for gefitinib. Firmonertinib's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier was also demonstrated in this clinical trial with a central nervous system (CNS) metastases specific ORR, which measured reduction of tumor size of at least 30% in brain metastases if present at the start of therapy, of 91% versus 65% for gefitinib. Based on observed clinical activity against exon 20 insertions in the FAVOUR clinical trial and observed activity against PACC mutations in the FURTHER clinical trial, we believe firmonertinib is potentially differentiated from third-generation EGFR TKIs approved for classical EGFRm NSCLC.

In the United States and the European Union, standard of care for first-line therapy in EGFRm NSCLC involving exon 20 insertion mutations is platinum-based chemotherapy with pemetrexed with or without amivantamab. These regimens have significantly lower response rates and DOR compared to results achieved in first-line patients with classical EGFRm who can be treated with approved third-generation EGFR TKIs. Over 9% of EGFRm NSCLC patients are estimated to have exon 20 insertion mutations. However, amivantamab appears to lack brain penetrance to effectively treat brain metastasis. In March 2024 and July 2024, amivantamab in combination with chemotherapy, was approved in the United States and Europe, respectively, for first line EGFRm NSCLC patients with exon 20 insertion mutations. However, amivantamab is an intravenously administered biologic lacking the advantages of oral therapies. Furthermore, amivantamab is being dosed in combination with chemotherapy in this setting with chemotherapy associated toxicities. We believe firmonertinib, if approved, has the potential to become a chemotherapy-free oral regimen in first-line EGFRm NSCLC patients with exon 20 insertion mutations given the clinical data generated in this patient population to date.

Guidelines employing TKIs for the treatment of many of the PACC EGFRm are not established and, as a result, chemotherapy is often used as the default course of therapy, offering limited efficacy and introducing chemotherapy-related toxicity. Afatinib (GILOTRIF®), a second-generation TKI, is also used in some patients, but has an unfavorable safety profile and is not brain penetrant. Osimertinib is frequently used in some patients, but the activity of osimertinib in such patients is less than its activity in patients with classical EGFRm NSCLC. Over 12% of EGFRm NSCLC patients are estimated to have PACC mutations. If approved, we believe firmonertinib has the potential to become a leading treatment option for first-line EGFRm NSCLC patients with PACC mutations based on firmonertinib's preclinical and clinical activity observed against these mutations and the evaluation of firmonertinib in multiple clinical trials.

We have designed a robust global clinical development plan across a broad spectrum of EGFRm NSCLC patient populations for which we believe firmonertinib will have a differentiated profile compared to currently available treatments. paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, the section of this Annual Report titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report, before investing in our common stock. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face.

Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of, or that we currently believe are not material, may also become important factors that affect us. If any of the following risks occur, our business, operating results and prospects could be materially harmed. In that event, the price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose part or all of your investment. This Annual Report also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. See "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements." Our actual results could differ materially and adversely from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors, including those set forth below.

Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, including those highlighted in this section below, that represent challenges that we face in connection with the successful implementation of our strategy. The occurrence of one or more of the events or circumstances described in more detail in the risk factors below, alone or in combination with other events or circumstances, may have an adverse effect on our business, cash flows, financial condition, and results of operations. Such risks include, but are not limited to:

● We have incurred significant operating losses since our inception and expect to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future. We are not currently profitable, and may never achieve or sustain profitability. If we are unable to achieve or sustain profitability, the market value of our common stock will likely decline.
● We have a limited operating history and no history of commercializing pharmaceutical products, which may make it difficult to evaluate the prospects for our future viability.

● Operating our business requires substantial additional capital to finance our goals, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our development programs, commercialization efforts or other operations.

We have entered into the Allist License Agreement, pursuant to which, we have, among other things, secured an exclusive, royalty bearing and sublicensable license under certain intellectual property, including patents and know-how, owned or controlled by Allist to develop and commercialize any product containing firmonertinib or any of its salts or derivatives as an active ingredient of a product, which is led by a joint collaboration committee, comprising of representatives from both Allist and us. Under the Allist License Agreement, we are obligated to pay Allist milestone payments up to an aggregate of $765.0 million upon the achievement of certain development, regulatory and sales milestone events as set forth in the Allist License Agreement. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we incurred $5.0 million in clinical milestones to Allist. We are also obligated under the Allist License Agreement to pay Allist tiered royalties based on net sales of Licensed Products (as defined in the Allist License Agreement). See "Business — Licenses, Partnerships and Collaborations — Allist Agreements."

Further, we are obligated to pay Lepu Biopharma milestone payments up to an aggregate of approximately $1.17 billion upon the achievement of certain development, regulatory and sales milestone events as set forth in the Lepu Biopharma Agreement, as defined herein. We are also obligated under the Lepu Biopharma Agreement to pay Lepu Biopharma tiered royalties based on net sales of Licensed Products, as defined herein. See "Business — Licenses, Partnerships and Collaborations — Lepu Biopharma Agreement".

Since our inception in April 2021, we have devoted substantially all of our resources to organizing and staffing our company, acquiring the rights to develop firmonertinib, ARR-217, and clinical development of firmonertinib, business planning, raising capital, identifying potential product candidates, enhancing our intellectual property portfolio and undertaking research and clinical and preclinical studies for our development programs. We do not have any products approved for sale and have not generated any revenue from product sales or otherwise. We have funded our operations to date primarily through the private placement of convertible preferred stock and through our initial public offering of common stock in January 2024, our "at-the-market" offering, and our underwritten public offering of common stock and pre-funded warrants to purchase common stock in July 2025.

We have incurred significant operating losses since our inception and have not yet generated any revenue. Our net losses were $166.3 million and $80.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $404.6 million. Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year, depending on the timing of our preclinical studies, clinical trials and our expenditures on other research and development activities. We expect to continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future. We anticipate these losses will increase substantially as we:
● advance our product candidates through clinical trials; ● acquire or in-license additional product candidates;
● advance our preclinical programs to clinical trials; ● further invest in our pipeline; ● further support our external partners' manufacturing capabilities;
● seek regulatory approval for our product candidates; ● pursue commercialization of our product candidates;
● maintain, expand, protect and defend our intellectual property portfolio;

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，專注於識別、開發與商業化差異化藥物，以解決癌症患者未被滿足的醫療需求。本公司旨在運用團隊深厚的藥物開發經驗，以最大化本公司主要產品候選藥物 firmonertinib 的潛力，並推進新型治療藥物，如新一代單株抗體藥物偶聯物（antibody drug conjugates），例如 ARR-217（MRG007）的核准與商業化，用以治療罹患癌症的患者，初期重點為實質性腫瘤。firmonertinib 目前正在多項臨牀試驗中評估，針對非小細胞肺腺癌（NSCLC）中不同表皮生長因子受體（EGFR）突變（EGFRm）的患者。本公司正在進行 firmonertinib 的關鍵性第三期臨牀試驗，用以治療未曾接受治療（treatment naive）或第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，其突變為 exon 20 插入突變，並進行 firmonertinib 的關鍵性第三期臨牀試驗，用以治療第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，其突變為 P-loop 和-alpha-c-helix 壓縮（PACC）突變。本公司正在進行 ARR-217 的第一期臨牀試驗，用以治療無法手術切除的局部晚期或轉移性實質性腫瘤患者。

本公司於 2023 年 10 月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）頒發 Breakthrough Therapy Designation（BTD）用於 firmonertinib 治療第一線 EGFRm NSCLC 的 exon 20 插入突變，並於 2024 年 2 月獲 Orphan Drug Designation 用於治療 NSCLC 的 EGFRm 或人表皮生長因子受體 2（HER2）突變或人表皮生長因子受體 4（HER4）突變。產品候選藥物可獲得 BTD，如果初步臨牀證據顯示該產品候選藥物，單獨或與一種或多種其他藥物組合，可能在一個或多個臨牀重要終點上顯著改善現有治療，例如臨牀開發初期觀察到的顯著治療效果。對於獲得 BTD 的藥物，FDA 與申辦人之間的互動與溝通可協助識別最有效的開發路徑，不過 BTD 可能不會導致開發過程、審查或核准加快，也不會增加產品候選藥物最終獲得 FDA 核准任何適應症的機率。

2021 年，本公司自上海 Allist 藥品有限公司（Allist）取得 firmonertinib 全球開發與商業化的權利，唯中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣地區除外。firmonertinib 是一種正在開發的新型 EGFR 突變選擇性酪胺酸 kinase 抑制劑（TKI），用以治療 NSCLC 患者，其適用範圍涵蓋比目前核准的 EGFR TKI 更廣的 EGFR 突變（EGFRm）。目前 firmonertinib 僅由 Allist 在中國核准並商業流通，作為第一線治療用於經典 EGFRm NSCLC。FDA 尚未核准 firmonertinib 用於任何用途。本公司選擇 firmonertinib 進行全球開發，針對非經典、或罕見的突變，是基於在進行中的第一期臨牀試驗 FAVOUR 中，觀察到 10 名 EGFR exon 20 插入突變患者中有 7 名在接受 firmonertinib 治療後腫瘤體積顯著減少，以及在 PACC 突變（為罕見突變的一種）中觀察到的預臨牀活性。在 FAVOUR 試驗的後續中期資料分析中，觀察到 240 mg 一日一次的 firmonertinib 在第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者中，有 79% 的患者（n=22 名患者，共 28 名患者）觀察到腫瘤體積至少減少 30%。在 Phase 1b FURTHER 試驗的最終分析中，包含 EGFRm NSCLC 的 PACC 突變族羣，觀察到 240 mg 的 firmonertinib 在第一線治療中，中位無進步存活時間（mPFS）為 16.0 個月，確認的總體反應率（cORR）為 68.2%（n=15 名患者，共 22 名第一線患者，240 mg）與反應持續時間（DOR）為 14.6 個月，並確認 firmonertinib 在 CNS（中樞神經系統）中的反應，包括完全反應（CRs）。

作為全球最常見的癌症之一，肺癌對人類健康造成顯著的全球負擔，而 EGFRm NSCLC 則是其中影響較大的一部分。儘管在 EGFRm NSCLC 的治療領域已有進展，許多患者，特別是那些具有罕見突變（如 exon 20 插入或 PACC 突變）的患者，仍未能獲得現有治療的充分照顧。在 FAVOUR 試驗的中期資料分析中，觀察到 240 mg 一日一次的 firmonertinib 在第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者中，有 79% 的患者（n=22 名患者，共 28 名患者）觀察到腫瘤體積至少減少 30%。在基線時無進步證據的患者中，觀察到腫瘤體積減少。
實體腫瘤（RECIST）1.1 標準。此項減少量為本試驗中部分反應的門檻，並作為總體反應率（ORR）的判定標準，而 ORR 是本試驗的主要評估指標。在相同的中期數據分析中，觀察到 79% 的病患中位數 DOR 為 15.2 個月。中期結果可能無法反映最終結果；然而，我們認為這些中期臨牀結果突顯了 firmonertinib 在腫瘤含有罕見 EGFRm 的病患中的潛力。

我們目前正進行一項關鍵性的第三期臨牀試驗，名為 FURVENT 臨牀試驗，針對一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性非鱗狀 EGFRm NSCLC 病患，其具有 exon 20 插入突變，並預計於 2026 年中取得此試驗的頂線數據。此外，我們也進行一項關鍵性的第三期臨牀試驗，名為 ALPACCA 臨牀試驗，針對一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性非鱗狀 EGFRm NSCLC 病患，其具有 PACC 突變。2025 年 9 月，我們公佈的最終第一期 1b PACC 數據顯示，在 240 mg 給藥組的 22 名一線病患中，有 15 名（佔 68.2%）觀察到在基線值下至少減少 30% 的腫瘤體積，且無進展證據，根據 RECIST 1.1 標準衡量。這些病患的確認 mPFS 為 16.0 個月。

自 2021 年成立以來，我們透過全球網路與在商業交易方面的經驗，建立了強大的腫瘤學產品線。2021 年，我們自 Allist 獲得在全球範圍內開發與商業化 firmonertinib 的權利，唯獨不包含大中華地區，即包括中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣。同年，我們與 Aarvik Therapeutics, Inc.（Aarvik）簽訂研究合作協議（後經修訂），以利用其專屬的多目標、多價、位點特異性連結抗體平台，發現下一代抗體藥物連結物（ADCs），其活性與安全性優於單目標雙價 ADCs。2024 年，我們與 Jiangsu Alphamab Biopharmaceuticals Co., Ltd.（Alphamab），為 Alphamab Oncology 的全資子公司，簽訂合作協議，以發現、開發與商業化用於全球癌症治療的新一代 ADCs，唯獨不包含大中華地區，即包括中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣。2025 年 1 月，我們與 Lepu Biopharma Co. Ltd.（Lepu Biopharma）簽訂獨家授權協議（Lepu Biopharma 協議），根據此協議，Lepu Biopharma 授予我們開發與商業化 ARR-217（MRG007），一種針對 CD-H17 的 ADC，用於大中華地區以外的胃腸道癌症治療，即包括中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣。
我們計畫持續進行商業發展活動，以尋找目前尚未被核准治療方案充分覆蓋的創新療法。此更廣泛的策略包括評估研究合作、合作夥伴關係與授權安排，以擴展我們開發中差異化且下一代的腫瘤學資產的產品線。下表總結了我們目前的產品線，顯示各項產品最進展的開發階段：
NSCLC: 非小細胞肺癌; EGFR: 表皮生長因子受體; PACC: P-loop alpha-c 螺旋壓縮; TKI: 酪胺酸激酶抑制劑; BTD: 突破性療法指定; ADC: 抗體藥物偶聯物; GI Tumors: 消化道腫瘤; 1L: 首線治療; Global Ex-China: 全球，除中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣。

目前核准的 EGFR TKIs 已取得相當商業成功，並成為治療具有經典 EGFRm 的 NSCLC 患者之標準療法，這些患者約佔所有 EGFRm NSCLC 患者大約 69%。然而，許多這些療法，包括阿斯利康 plc 的（阿斯利康）第三代 EGFR TKI，奧希替尼（TAGRISSO®），對具有罕見 EGFRm 的 NSCLC 患者僅有微弱作用或未核准用於該部分患者。此未被滿足的醫療需求，使許多 EGFRm NSCLC 患者缺乏有效的治療選擇。Firmonertinib 目前已核准並由 Allist 在中國作為首線治療用以治療經典 EGFRm NSCLC。然而，Firmonertinib 被設計為對經典 EGFRm 以及罕見 EGFRm，例如 exon 20 插入和 PACC 突變，均有強烈的抑制作用，這些突變合計約佔 EGFRm NSCLC 約 22%。

截至目前為止，Firmonertinib 已在多項臨牀試驗中評估，總計超過 1,000 名患者，對廣泛的 EGFRm NSCLC，包括經典和罕見 EGFRm。根據迄今為止進行的預臨牀及臨牀試驗結果，我們認為 Firmonertinib 有潛力保留第三代 EGFR TKIs 相較於第一及第二代 EGFR TKIs 的許多關鍵優勢，包括克服 T790M 突變，這些突變會導致早期一代 TKIs 抵抗，同時也針對更廣泛的 EGFRm。2022 年，Allist 報告了其 FURLONG 臨牀試驗的結果，這是一項雙盲、安慰劑對照的第三期臨牀試驗，用以評估 Firmonertinib 在經典 EGFRm NSCLC 首線患者中的治療效果。在 FURLONG 試驗中，Firmonertinib 與第一代 EGFR TKI，吉非替尼，進行比較，並顯示出優於吉非替尼的進展自由生存期（PFS），顯示中位 PFS 為 20.8 個月，對照組吉非替尼為 11.1 個月。Firmonertinib 在此臨牀試驗中也顯示出能穿越血腦屏障的能力，具有一個中央神經系統（CNS）轉移專屬的反應率（ORR），測量在治療開始時若有腦轉移，腫瘤體積減少至少 30% 的比例為 91% 對照組吉非替尼為 65%。根據在 FAVOUR 臨牀試驗中觀察到對 exon 20 插入的臨牀活性，以及在 FURTHER 臨牀試驗中觀察到對 PACC 突變的活性，我們認為 Firmonertinib 有潛力與核准用於經典 EGFRm NSCLC 的第三代 EGFR TKIs 區別開來。

在美國和歐盟，針對 EGFRm NSCLC 涉及 exon 20 插入突變的首線治療，標準療法為含培美曲塞的鉑基化療，這些療法的反應率和持續反應時間（DOR）顯著低於首線治療經典 EGFRm 的患者，這些患者可使用核准的第三代 EGFR TKIs 治療。估計超過 9% 的 EGFRm NSCLC 患者具有 exon 20 插入突變。然而，阿美坦坦（amivantamab）似乎缺乏腦穿透能力，無法有效治療腦轉移。2024 年 3 月和 2024 年 7 月，阿美坦坦與化療聯合使用，在美國和歐盟分別核准用於首線 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，這些患者具有 exon 20 插入突變。然而，阿美坦坦是一種靜脈注射的生物製劑，缺乏口服療法的優勢。此外，在此情境下，阿美坦坦與化療聯合使用，而化療會導致毒性反應。我們認為，若 Firmonertinib 被核准，有潛力成為首線 EGFRm NSCLC 患者中具有 exon 20 插入突變的化療-free 口服療法，基於迄今為止在該患者羣體中產生的臨牀數據。

針對許多 PACC EGFRm 的 TKI 治療指南尚未建立，因此化療常被用作預設治療方式，提供有限的療效並引入化療相關毒性。阿法替尼（GILOTRIF®），一種第二代 TKI，也用於部分患者，但其安全性不佳且缺乏腦穿透能力。奧希替尼常被用於部分患者，但在這些患者中的活性低於其在經典 EGFRm NSCLC 患者中的活性。估計超過 12% 的 EGFRm NSCLC 患者具有 PACC 突變。若核准，我們認為 Firmonertinib 有潛力成為首線 EGFRm NSCLC 患者中具有 PACC 突變的首選治療選擇，基於 Firmonertinib 對這些突變的預臨牀及臨牀活性，以及 Firmonertinib 在多項臨牀試驗中的評估。
我們設計了一個強大的全球臨牀發展計畫，涵蓋廣泛的 EGFRm NSCLC 患者羣體，我們認為 Firmonertinib 將與現有治療相比具有差異化特徵。下表描述了我們或合作夥伴進行的 Firmonertinib 主要計畫及進行中的臨牀試驗：

paragraphs: 您應閱讀以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，並與本年度財務報表及相關附註一同參考。本討論與分析中包含的部分資訊，包括有關我們業務與相關融資的計畫與策略，包含風險與不確定性。由於許多因素，包括本年度財務報告中「風險因素」部分所列的因素，我們的實際結果可能與討論與分析中所描述或暗示的預測結果有顯著差異。您應仔細閱讀本年度財務報告中的「風險因素」部分，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與我們預測結果有顯著差異的重要因素。請同時參閱標題為「關於前瞻性陳述的特別說明」的節錄。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物製藥公司，致力於識別、開發與商業化差異化的藥物，以解決癌症患者未被滿足的醫療需求。我們旨在利用我們團隊深厚的藥物開發經驗，以最大化我們領先產品候選藥物 firmonertinib 的潛力，並推進一連串創新治療藥物的開發，例如下一代抗體藥物偶聯物，包括 ARR-217 (MRG007)，透過核准與商業化，用以治療罹患癌症的患者，初期重點為實體腫瘤。Firmonertinib 目前正在多項臨牀試驗中評估，用於不同類型的 EGFRm 在非小細胞肺癌 (NSCLC) 中的應用。我們正在進行 firmonertinib 的關鍵 III 期臨牀試驗，用於治療未接受過治療、或第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，這些患者具有 exon 20 插入突變，並進行 firmonertinib 的關鍵 III 期臨牀試驗，
用於治療第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，這些患者具有 PACC 突變。我們同時也在進行 ARR-217 的 I 期臨牀試驗，用於治療無法手術切除的局部晚期或轉移性實體腫瘤患者。

我們在 2023 年 10 月從美國食品藥物管理局 (FDA) 獲得 firmonertinib 的突破性療法指定，用於第一線治療 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，這些患者具有 exon 20 插入突變。我們在 2024 年 2 月獲得治療 NSCLC 患者具有 EGFRm 或 HER2 突變或 HER4 突變的罕見藥物指定。產品候選藥物可獲得 BTD 指定，如果初步臨牀證據顯示該產品候選藥物，單獨或與一種或多種其他藥物組合，可能在一個或更多臨牀重要終點上顯示出顯著改善，例如臨牀開發早期觀察到的顯著治療效果。對於被指定為突破性療法的藥物，FDA 與申辦人的互動與溝通可幫助識別最有效的開發路徑，雖然 BTD 可能不會導致更快的開發過程、審查或核准，也不會增加產品候選藥物最終獲得 FDA 核准的機率。

2021 年，我們從 Allist 獲得在全球範圍內開發與商業化 firmonertinib 的權利，除外中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣地區。Firmonertinib 是一種正在開發的新型 EGFR 突變選擇性 TKI，我們正在開發用以治療 NSCLC 患者，其 EGFRm 覆蓋範圍比目前核准的 EGFR TKI 更廣。目前 firmonertinib 僅由 Allist 在中國核准並商業化，作為第一線治療經典 EGFRm NSCLC 的藥物。美國食品藥物管理局 (FDA) 尚未核准 firmonertinib 用於任何用途。我們選擇 firmonertinib 進行全球開發，針對非經典、或罕見的突變，是基於在進行中的 Phase 1b 臨牀試驗 FAVOUR 中，觀察到七名十名具有 EGFR exon 20 插入突變的患者在接受 firmonertinib 治療後，腫瘤體積減小。此試驗由 Allist 在中國進行，並觀察到預臨牀活動在 PACC 突變中，每種都是罕見突變的一種類型。在 FAVOUR 試驗的後續中期數據分析中，針對第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，這些患者具有 exon 20 插入突變，並接受每日 240 mg 的 firmonertinib 治療，觀察到 79% 的患者（n=22 名患者，共 28 名患者）腫瘤體積減小至少 30%。在 Phase 1B FURTHER 試驗的最終分析中，針對包含 EGFRm NSCLC 的 PACC 突變羣組，我們觀察到 firmonertinib 240 mg 的 mPFS 為 16.0 個月，cORR 為 68.2%（n=15 名患者，共 22 名第一線患者，每日 240 mg），DOR 為 14.6 個月，並確認 firmonertinib 在 CNS 中的反應，包括完全反應 (CRs)。

作為全球最常見的癌症之一，肺癌對人類健康造成顯著的全球負擔，而 EGFRm NSCLC 佔據了這些患者中的一大部分。儘管在 EGFRm NSCLC 的治療領域已有進展，但許多患者，特別是那些具有罕見突變，如 exon 20 插入或 PACC 突變的患者，仍然未被現有治療方案充分照顧。在 FAVOUR 試驗的中期數據分析中，針對第一線治療的局部晚期或轉移性 EGFRm NSCLC 患者，這些患者具有 exon 20 插入突變，觀察到 79% 的患者（n=22 名患者，共 28 名患者）在接受每日 240 mg 的 firmonertinib 治療後，腫瘤體積從基線減少至少 30%，且在 RECIST 1.1 標準下，未顯示疾病進展。此減少量是此試驗中部分反應的門檻，也是此試驗中確定 ORR（主要終點）的條件。在相同的中期數據分析中，這 79% 的患者觀察到 15.2 個月的中位 DOR。中期結果可能無法代表最終結果；然而，我們認為這些中期臨牀結果突顯了 firmonertinib 在具有罕見 EGFRm 腫瘤患者的潛力。

我們已與 Allist 簽訂許可協議，根據此協議，我們已取得某些智慧財產權，包括專利與技術知識，由 Allist 擁有或控制的獨家、附帶版稅且可轉讓的許可，用以開發與商業化任何含有 firmonertinib 或其鹽類或衍生物作為活性成分的產品，此產品由雙方代表組成的共同合作委員會領導。根據 Allist 許可協議，我們有義務支付 Allist 里程碑付款，總計達 765.0 百萬美元，以達成協議中所列的開發、監管與銷售里程碑事件。在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結訖的會計年度中，我們支付給 Allist 5.0 百萬美元的臨牀里程碑付款。我們根據 Allist 許可協議，也有義務支付 Allist 基於銷售核准產品的階梯式版稅。請參閱「業務—許可、合作與合作夥伴關係—Allist 協議」。

我們已與 Lepu Biopharma 簽訂協議，根據此協議，我們已取得某些智慧財產權，包括專利與技術知識，由 Lepu Biopharma 擁有或控制的獨家、附帶版稅且可轉讓的許可，用以開發與商業化任何含有 ARR-217 或 ARR-217 的抗體組分的產品。此外，我們有義務支付 Lepu Biopharma 里程碑付款，總計達約 11.7 億美元，以達成協議中所列的開發、監管與銷售里程碑事件。我們根據 Lepu Biopharma 協議，也有義務支付 Lepu Biopharma 基於銷售核准產品的階梯式版稅。請參閱「業務—許可、合作與合作夥伴關係—Lepu Biopharma 協議」。

自2021年4月成立以來，本公司已將 substantially all 的資源投入於組織與人力配置本公司、取得開發 firmonertinib、ARR-217 及 firmonertinib 臨牀開發之權利、商業規劃、籌措資金、尋找潛在產品候選物、強化智慧財產權組合，以及進行開發計畫之研究與臨牀及前期臨牀研究。本公司目前尚無任何已核准銷售之產品，亦未自產品銷售或其他方式產生任何收入。本公司至今主要透過私募可轉換優先股發行及2024年1月首次公開發行普通股、"at-the-market" 發行、以及2025年7月的經承銷公開發行普通股及預資 warrants 購買普通股資金支應營運。
自本公司成立以來，已產生顯著之營運虧損，且尚未產生任何收入。本公司2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日之淨虧損分別為166.3 百萬美元及80.5 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為404.6 百萬美元。本公司淨虧損可能因前期臨牀研究、臨牀試驗及其它研究與開發活動之支出時程而顯著波動。本公司預期將在可預見之未來持續產生虧損。本公司預期這些虧損將顯著增加，因：
● 推進產品候選物通過臨牀試驗； ● 收購或授權取得其他產品候選物；
● 推進前期臨牀計畫至臨牀試驗； ● 進一步投資於本公司產品管線； ● 進一步支援外部夥伴之製造能力；
● 尋求產品候選物之監管核准； ● 推進產品候選物之商業化；
● 維持、擴展、保護及防禦本公司智慧財產權組合；

與我們產品候選藥物的開發及監管審批相關的風險
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性、本年度報告中標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」的章節，以及我們財務報表及相關附註，再決定是否投資本公司普通股。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險。

我們可能還會面臨其他未預見或目前認為不具重大影響的風險與不確定性，這些因素也可能成為影響我們的重要因素。若任何下列風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、營運成果與前景造成重大損害。在此情況下，本公司普通股的價格可能下跌，您可能損失部分或全部投資。本年度報告中亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。請參閱「關於展望性陳述之特別說明」。我們實際的結果可能與這些展望性陳述中預期的結果有重大且不利的差異，原因包括下列所列因素。
我們的業務面臨許多風險與不確定性，包括本節下列所強調的風險，這些風險代表我們在成功執行策略時所面臨的挑戰。下列風險因素中所詳細說明的事件或情況，單獨或與其他事件或情況結合發生，可能對我們的業務、現金流、財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。這些風險包括但不限於：
● 自我們成立以來，我們已產生重大營運虧損，並預期在可預見的未來持續產生重大虧損。我們目前尚未獲利，且可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。若我們無法達成或維持獲利，本公司普通股的市場價值將可能下跌。
● 我們的營運歷史有限，且沒有商業化製藥產品的經驗，這可能使評估我們未來生存前景變得困難。
● 運作我們的業務需要大量額外資金以實現我們的目標，若無法在需要時以可接受的條件或完全無法取得此必要資金，將迫使我們延遲、限制、減少或終止我們的開發計畫、商業化努力或其他業務運作。
